rows.relationship: Galena and sphalerite in quartz point to a lead-zinc-silver vein system.
Quartz with pyrite indicates hot fluids moved through the rock — a hydrothermal system that is worth examining for metals.
Scheelite in quartz (fluorescing blue under UV) indicates a tungsten-bearing vein or skarn.
Cassiterite with tourmaline signals a greisen or evolved-granite system carrying tin (and often tungsten).
Chromite with olivine marks an ultramafic body — a setting for chromium, nickel and platinum-group metals.
Green malachite and blue azurite are the oxidised cap of a copper system — follow it down to primary chalcopyrite.
Pyrope garnet with chrome diopside is the classic mantle-indicator suite geologists use to trace kimberlite and diamond potential.
Calc-silicate garnet and pyroxene indicate a skarn at an intrusive-carbonate contact, which may host tungsten, copper or iron.
Spodumene with lepidolite is diagnostic of a lithium-rich (LCT) pegmatite.
Bastnaesite and monazite together indicate rare-earth mineralisation, typically in a carbonatite or alkaline complex.
Chalcopyrite with bornite indicates primary copper sulphide mineralisation, typical of porphyry and skarn systems.
Arsenopyrite with quartz is a well-known pathfinder for orogenic gold; gold often sits with or near arsenopyrite.
